title: Resolver Phase 0: wire parent_symbol_id through to resolution
description:
Near-free win pulled out of the scope-aware resolution design; independent of the Phase A architecture work and can ship immediately.

Fact: parent_symbol_id is persisted on every symbol row (db/mod.rs:246, populated at insert, mod.rs:786) and fetched by find_symbols_by_file — but silently discarded before resolution: pipeline.rs:304 hardcodes children: vec![] when reconstructing ExtractedSymbol from SQL, and all_symbols_summary (db/mod.rs:1219-1228) selects only (id, qualified_name, short_name, kind), dropping both parent_symbol_id and file_path.

Change:
1. Widen all_symbols_summary / the resolver's symbol structures to carry parent_symbol_id (and file_path while there — the global fallback currently can't even prefer same-file candidates).
2. pick_nearest_local (resolver.rs:152-173): prefer definitions whose parent chain contains the reference's enclosing symbol (enclosing-scope-chain preference) before falling back to the current line-proximity heuristic. This fixes a class of shadowing/nesting misresolutions with zero parser changes.
3. Extend tests/resolver_test.rs with nested-scope fixtures: method in impl vs same-named free function; inner fn shadowing outer name; same-file preference in global fallback.

No schema changes, no parser changes — purely resolution-pass plumbing. Contract note: resolution results will change for currently-misresolved refs (that's the point); rerun the full resolver test suite and spot-check graph edge diffs on sutra's own index before/after.

decisions.decision: Used line-range containment for scope preference instead of parent_symbol_id chain walking
decisions.rationale: Line ranges are available on every ExtractedSymbol without DB id lookups; parent_symbol_id requires mapping DB ids back to symbols which adds complexity for no benefit at the file-local level. parent_symbol_id is still wired through for future cross-file scope resolution.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Walk parent_symbol_id chains via HashMap<i64, &ExtractedSymbol> — adds allocation and lookup overhead for equivalent results within a single file.

decisions.decision: Named the new struct SymbolEntry instead of SymbolSummary
decisions.rationale: db::similarity::SymbolSummary already exists with different fields; collision caused compilation errors.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Rename the similarity type — higher blast radius, touches unrelated code.

execution_record: Three commits: 6576c69 (plumbing + resolver logic), fadd18d (tests), a5c49bb (codex review fixes). SymbolEntry struct replaces the (i64,String,String,String) tuple — originally named SymbolSummary but renamed to avoid collision with db::similarity::SymbolSummary. Scope preference uses line-range containment (tightest_common_scope_size) rather than walking parent_symbol_id chains. Codex adversarial review caught two bugs: (1) local→global lookup didn't filter by file_id so duplicate qualified_names across files could bind wrong, (2) scope exclusion used line-range equality which could drop real enclosing scopes. Both fixed with regression tests."

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex review: needs-attention → fixed in a5c49bb.

1. [high] Local resolution ignored file_id when mapping local symbol to DB row — could bind to wrong file for duplicate qn. Fixed: added file_id filter.
2. [medium] Scope exclusion used line-range equality which could drop real enclosing scopes sharing the same range. Fixed: use qualified_name identity.

Both findings have regression tests."
